comment: Per-work assignment to a genre cluster. Each cluster has a curated public-domain Latin/English parallel anchor set; the harness loads the cluster-appropriate index when translating a work. See METHODOLOGY.md §5.2 (v1/v2 note) for the licensing rationale.

crypto-occult.description: Cryptographic, hermetic, demonological, and angelological works. Includes the Polygraphia treatises, the Clavis works, the Sigilla, and the Liber Octo Quaestionum (responses to Maximilian on witchcraft).
anchor_sources_pd: Henry Cornelius Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, tr. JF (London, 1651) — public domain. Latin source: De Occulta Philosophia (Cologne, 1533).
William Lilly, Of the Seven Secondary Causes / De Septem Secundeis (London, 1647) — public domain. Trithemius's own text in his own century's English.
G.R.S. Mead, Thrice-Greatest Hermes (Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906) — public domain. Hermetica with Latin/Greek source apparatus.
Meric Casaubon, A True & Faithful Relation of What Passed for Many Yeers Between Dr. John Dee and Some Spirits (London, 1659) — public domain. Latin and English passages in close proximity.
crypto-occult.register_notes: Late-medieval scholastic Latin with spirit-prince names, angelological tables, and conjuration formulae. Anchors should preserve technical magical vocabulary and Latin word-order in invocations.

bibliographic.description: Catalog and biographical works — De Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis and the Spanheim/Würzburg collected-works compilations and chronicles.
anchor_sources_pd: Jerome, De Viris Illustribus, tr. Ernest Cushing Richardson in NPNF Series II, vol. III (1892) — public domain. Directly comparable genre (catalog of ecclesiastical writers).
Gennadius of Marseille, De Viris Illustribus (continuation), tr. Ernest Cushing Richardson in NPNF Series II, vol. III (1892) — public domain.
Bede, Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum, tr. A. M. Sellar (London, 1907) — public domain. For chronicle register.
Isidore of Seville, De Viris Illustribus, in older PD editions of his collected works.
bibliographic.register_notes: Terse biographical entries; lists of works with incipits; chronological framing.

monastic-reform.description: Works on monastic observance, the state of the orders, claustral life, exhortations to monks, and chapter resolutions. Includes De Laude Scriptorum Manualium (manuscript culture is a monastic register).
anchor_sources_pd: John Cassian, Institutes and Conferences, tr. Edgar Gibson in NPNF Series II, vol. XI (1894) — public domain. The foundational text of Western monastic register.
Athanasius, Life of Antony, tr. Robertson in NPNF Series II, vol. IV (1892) — public domain.
Sulpitius Severus, Life of St. Martin, tr. Roberts in NPNF Series II, vol. XI (1894) — public domain.
Rule of St. Benedict — pre-1929 PD English translations available (e.g. Boniface Verheyen OSB, 1949 is post-1929 but earlier 19th-c. translations are PD; the Migne Latin is always PD).
monastic-reform.register_notes: Hortatory, scriptural-quotation-heavy, frequent appeals to the Desert Fathers and Benedictine rule.

sacerdotal.description: Pastoral and priestly works — pastoral care, the formation of priests, the priestly vocation.
anchor_sources_pd: Gregory the Great, Liber Regulae Pastoralis (Book of Pastoral Rule), tr. James Barmby in NPNF Series II, vol. XII (1895) — public domain. The canonical Latin pastoral manual.
Augustine, De Doctrina Christiana (On Christian Doctrine), tr. J. F. Shaw in NPNF Series I, vol. II (1887) — public domain.
sacerdotal.register_notes: Practical-doctrinal, addressing the priest's formation, duties, and the cure of souls.

marian-hagiographic.description: Marian devotion (especially the Anne / immaculate-conception tradition), Carmelite hagiography.
anchor_sources_pd: Bernard of Clairvaux, Sermones in laudibus Virginis Matris and other Marian sermons, tr. Samuel J. Eales (London, 1895) — public domain.
Anselm of Canterbury, Prayers and Meditations (including Marian prayers), in pre-1929 English editions — public domain.
Augustine, Marian-context sermons in NPNF Series I (1886-1888) — public domain.
marian-hagiographic.register_notes: Hymnic; high-register; frequent epithets, anaphora, and citations of the Song of Songs and Psalms.

devotional.description: Contemplative and ascetic works — divine love, the vanity of human life, conversion of the mind to God.
anchor_sources_pd: Bernard of Clairvaux, De Diligendo Deo (On Loving God), tr. Edmund Garratt Gardner (London, 1916) — public domain.
Augustine, Confessions, tr. E. B. Pusey (London, 1838) — public domain.
Thomas à Kempis, De Imitatione Christi, in pre-1929 English editions (Whitford 1556, Stanhope 1696, Knox 1853, etc.) — public domain.
devotional.register_notes: First-person interior; addresses the soul or God directly; Augustinian and Bernardine vocabulary of caritas, contritio, conversio.

apologetic.description: Self-defense / apologetic works (one work: Sui Ipsius Vindex).
anchor_sources_pd: Augustine, Retractationes (Retractations), in NPNF Series I, vol. I (1886) — public domain.
Jerome, apologetic letters and Adversus Rufinum, in NPNF Series II, vol. III (1892) — public domain.
apologetic.register_notes: Defensive-polemical; first-person; cites past works and rebuts critics.

verse.description: Occasional Latin verse (one work: the bald-men ecloga to Maximilian).
anchor_sources_pd: Hucbald of St. Amand, Ecloga de Calvis, in Thomas Wright, ed., Latin Poems Commonly Attributed to Walter Mapes (Camden Society, 1841) — public domain. Direct predecessor of Trithemius's poem.
Erasmus, Encomium Moriae (Praise of Folly), tr. White Kennett (1683) or Wilson (1668) — public domain. Renaissance satirical Latin verse register.
Bucolic / pastoral PD English of Virgil's Eclogues (Dryden 1697, etc.) for the eclogue form itself.
verse.register_notes: Encomiastic-satirical; metric (hexameter or elegiacs); rhetorical praise of an unworthy subject as comedic device.
